title: Bilum looped string bag
summary: A bilum is looped from twisted plant string, row after row, by hand and without a loom. Colours are worked in bands and steps into the open loops. Copy the pattern, which mirrors left to right.
howToPlay: Pick a string colour and a pattern shape.
Place it; the mirror partner is looped too.
Check the bag against the pattern.
Watch and learn shows a finished round, one placement at a time.
rules: The bag mirrors left to right.
Placing the same shape in the same colour again, or choosing the eraser, clears it and its mirror partners.
The result compares your piece with the pattern cell by cell: three stars at 98 percent or more, two at 85, one at 60.
The pattern to copy is always shown beside the work and as a faint guide on the cloth.
heritageNote: The bilum is the looped string bag of Papua New Guinea, made in many regions by hand from twisted plant fibre or wool, carried for produce and children and worn as a sign of belonging. Colours and patterns differ between communities.
credits: Pattern designs are original arrangements in the tradition's motif vocabulary.
